external_entities.name: Member
external_entities.description: A person who uses the loyalty programme, mobile app, and partner apps.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Members collect points when they shop and spend them on gift cards.
external_entities.notes: The text does not state where the member is located.

external_entities.name: Member phone
external_entities.description: A member's phone running the mobile app and holding a refresh token.
external_entities.source_excerpt: The app keeps a refresh token on the phone.
external_entities.notes: The phone is outside the organisation's cloud account.

external_entities.name: Member browser
external_entities.description: The browser used by a member to sign in and approve partner-app consent.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A member who connects a partner app signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser
external_entities.notes: The text does not explicitly place the browser in a zone.

external_entities.name: Partner app
external_entities.description: A web application operated by another company that accesses loyalty data for a member.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Partner apps are web applications that other companies run on their own servers
external_entities.notes: The partner app is outside the organisation's control and runs on the other company's own server.

processes.name: Mobile app
processes.description: The organisation's mobile app, which signs members in, stores a refresh token on the phone, and calls the rewards API.
processes.source_excerpt: Members use our mobile app. The app signs a member in through our authorization server with the authorization code flow and then calls the rewards API
processes.notes: The text says it is unknown whether the app sends a PKCE challenge. The mobile refresh token never expires; each use slides its expiry forward another ninety days.

processes.name: Authorization server
processes.description: The server that authenticates members, handles authorization-code flows and consent, and issues access and refresh tokens.
processes.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database
processes.notes: The authorization server signs tokens for the support console with the same key used for other tokens.

processes.name: Rewards API
processes.description: The API that reads and writes the points ledger, redeems points for gift cards, and logs requests.
processes.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger
processes.notes: It does not check which client or audience an access token was issued for.

processes.name: Support console
processes.description: A web application used to close a member's account.
processes.source_excerpt: The support console is a web app that closes a member's account.
processes.notes: It is served on the same public hostname as the rewards API.

data_stores.name: Identity database
data_stores.description: The database holding member identity data and authorization-server-issued codes, tokens, and consents.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database, together with the authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents it issues.
data_stores.notes: The database also retains refresh tokens after a member account is closed. Protection at rest is not recorded.

data_stores.name: Points ledger
data_stores.description: The ledger holding every member's balance and every points transaction.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger, which holds every member's balance and every points transaction.
data_stores.notes: Protection at rest is not recorded.

data_stores.name: API log store
data_stores.description: The store receiving every request received by the rewards API, including headers.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.
data_stores.notes: Protection at rest is not recorded.

data_flows.name: use mobile app
data_flows.description: A member phone uses the mobile app.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Members use our mobile app.
data_flows.notes: The connection from the phone uses HTTPS.

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: The mobile app signs a member in through the authorization server using the authorization code flow.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app signs a member in through our authorization server with the authorization code flow
data_flows.notes: It is unknown whether the app sends a PKCE challenge.

data_flows.name: call rewards API
data_flows.description: The mobile app calls the rewards API with an access token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: then calls the rewards API with the access token it gets back
data_flows.notes: The connection from a phone uses HTTPS. The access token is a plain bearer token and lives for one hour.

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: A member's browser accesses the authorization server sign-in page.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A member who connects a partner app signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser
data_flows.notes: The connection from a browser uses HTTPS. The sign-in cookie is kept for thirty days and no idle timeout was decided.

data_flows.name: return code
data_flows.description: The browser returns an authorization code to the partner app's redirect URI.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The browser then returns to the partner app's redirect URI with an authorization code.
data_flows.notes: The connection from a browser uses HTTPS.

data_flows.name: request tokens
data_flows.description: A partner app sends token requests containing its client secret to the authorization server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The partner app sends that secret in the body of its token requests.
data_flows.notes: The connection from a partner server uses HTTPS. Every partner app is given every scope.
data_flows.data_description: client ID, client secret, authorization code, scopes, and token request data

data_flows.name: take access token
data_flows.description: The support console takes access tokens from the authorization server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It takes access tokens from the same authorization server
data_flows.notes: The connection from a browser or partner server uses HTTPS; the text does not specify the support console's connection details.

data_flows.name: store identity data
data_flows.description: The authorization server stores member and authorization data in the identity database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database, together with the authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents it issues.
data_flows.notes: The connection protection is not recorded.
data_flows.data_description: member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, and consents

data_flows.name: read-write ledger
data_flows.description: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger
data_flows.notes: How the rewards API connects to the ledger is not recorded.

data_flows.name: write request logs
data_flows.description: The rewards API writes each received request and its headers to the API log store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.
data_flows.notes: How the rewards API connects to the API log store is not recorded.

data_flows.name: close account
data_flows.description: The support console marks a member's account closed in the identity database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Closing an account marks it closed in the identity database.
data_flows.notes: How the support console connects to the identity database is not recorded.

trust_boundaries.name: Own cloud account
trust_boundaries.description: The organisation's cloud account where the platform components run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Everything below runs in our own cloud account
trust_boundaries.notes: The text does not describe the network segmentation or privilege arrangement within the cloud account.

trust_boundaries.name: Members' phones
trust_boundaries.description: The zone containing members' phones, which are outside the organisation's cloud account.
trust_boundaries.notes: The text places phones outside the organisation's cloud account but does not describe their network arrangement.

trust_boundaries.name: Partner apps' own servers
trust_boundaries.description: The zone containing partner applications operated by other companies on their own servers.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: partner apps that other companies run on their own servers
trust_boundaries.notes: The partner servers are controlled by other companies.

assumptions.assumption: The authorization server is reachable from the internet because members' browsers and partner servers connect to it.
assumptions.basis: The text describes browser sign-in and partner-server token requests to the authorization server, and states that connections from browsers and partner servers use HTTPS.

assumptions.assumption: The rewards API is internet-facing because it is served on a public hostname and is called by the mobile app.
assumptions.basis: The text says the support console is served on the same public hostname as the rewards API and that the mobile app calls the rewards API.

assumptions.assumption: The support console is internet-facing because it is served on a public hostname.
assumptions.basis: The text says the support console is served on the same public hostname as the rewards API.

assumptions.assumption: The identity database is confidential because it holds member identity data, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, and consents.
assumptions.basis: The stated contents include email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, and consents.

assumptions.assumption: The points ledger is confidential because it holds member balances and points transactions.
assumptions.basis: The stated contents include every member's balance and every points transaction.

assumptions.assumption: The API log store is confidential because it holds every request and its headers, which can include credentials and personal or operational data.
assumptions.basis: The text states that every request received by the rewards API, headers included, is written to the API log store.
